title: Semantic Search: Finding Meaning Instead of Exact Words
headline:
Search for meaning,
not just matching words.
meaning: Embeddings represent content as numerical vectors.
example: A query about a rainy trip may find a relevant note.
comparison: Similar meaning can match different wording.
caution: Similarity does not guarantee truth or relevance.
question: When would meaning-based search help?
lines: You search for a rainy trip, but the note says wet weekend. Exact word matching might miss the connection.
Semantic search uses embeddings: numerical representations that capture useful relationships between pieces of content.
A query and a document can be compared in that numerical space, even when their wording differs.
This helps retrieve related material. Some systems can compare images, audio, or video as well as text.
Similarity is not a guarantee of truth. Inspect the results and test how the search behaves.
